prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Offshore wind O&M; scope Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere), excludes public grid and non-farm port ops. Wildmere: Export Limit Advisory→Grid Dispatcher when capability<target; applies accepted ceiling, records time; keeps protection settings unless authorized switching plan; stays available for protection/control during substation work. Turbine Controller (Glassfin): validated commands within protections, blocks conflicts, safe mode on auxiliary loss; Pitch Deviation Notice. Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor→Turbine Sensor Bus. Substation Operator switches after state check + Control Engineer authorization, notifies Grid Dispatcher, confirms switching sequence fits window. Emergency Generator (Foxglove): auto-start on auxiliary loss, no unapproved paralleling; Start Test Trace. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale): telemetry→Shore Control Room (Amber Quay); Session Revocation Receipt→Cybersecurity Gateway. Shore Control Room keeps last validated limit on comms loss; Switching Window Acknowledgment; incident log; go/no-go. Grid Dispatcher priority safety>protection>export; confirms window vs export/network limits. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard): Position Quality Flag. Mode Grid Constraint: Duty Planner records basis; Control Engineer reduces stepwise, restores after authorization. Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown): Squall Window Bulletin, Deferred Task Rationale, replenishment forecasts; checks durations/dependencies/resources before window proposal. Weather Service→Weather Analyst (Wave Burst Record, Visibility Confidence Note)→Duty Planner; Metocean Buoy. Uncertain=no-go; Blade Inspection Drone deferred. Vessel Master proceed/hold/withdraw; Transfer Manifest Addendum from Duty Planner. CTV (Harness Audit Card), Daughter Craft, SOV (Recovery Basket Load Sheet); Marine Coordinator. North/South Access Scanner, Personnel Tracking Console; discrepancy pauses transfers. SCADA Engineer verifies Firmware Hash Attestation. Emergency: Rescue Coordinator, Field Supervisor, HSE Officer; Control Engineer remote shutdown; mode Turbine Lockout. Inventory: Warehouse System authoritative; Spares Hub; Storekeeper reconciles; substitutions need engineering acceptance. Isolation: approved boundary; lock/tag, PPE, tested voltage-absence checks, stored energy assessed; Field Supervisor briefs limits; changes→boundary review; Work Permit Portal keeps current approval, voids superseded; same revision

Document units:
S745: Export capacity is assessed before any planned outage that could restrict power transfer.
S746: A Grid Constraint may require the requested window to be shortened, moved, or divided into separate periods.
S747: The final window allows time for switching, work execution, testing, and restoration without relying on unplanned extensions.
S748: Weather Service forecasts are considered when marine access or external work affects the achievable start time.
S749: The Marine Coordinator checks vessel movements and crew transfer timing against the proposed period.
S750: The Electrical Technician confirms that the work scope and test requirements fit the approved duration.
S751: The Work Permit Portal is updated to reflect the agreed timing and work boundaries before the activity begins.
S752: Offshore Substation uses the Switching Window Acknowledgment to confirm that the approved switching window is available for the planned work.
S753: The Substation Operator does not begin switching until the window is active and operational authority has been confirmed.
S754: Any delay that threatens the agreed end time is raised promptly for review by the responsible operations staff.
S755: Work is paused if actual conditions make the planned sequence unsafe or incompatible with grid requirements.
S756: A revised window is agreed before deferred switching or additional maintenance is attempted.
S757: Following completion, equipment is restored in the authorized sequence and its operating condition is checked.
S758: The Duty Planner records actual start and finish times to improve future estimates and coordination.
S759: Substation availability is returned to the operating plan only after restoration checks are complete and any remaining limitations are understood.
S760: Operational communications support safe decisions by providing timely, clear, and traceable information to the people responsible for offshore work.
S761: The Shore Control Room is the coordination point for routine operational messages between shore-based personnel and offshore teams.
S762: The Operations Radio Console supports voice communication with the Crew Transfer Vessel, Service Operations Vessel, and Daughter Craft when they are within radio coverage.
S763: The Vessel Master confirms safety-critical instructions using the agreed read-back procedure before the vessel acts on them.
S764: The Marine Coordinator shares relevant marine and weather information with vessel personnel and the Duty Planner.
S765: The Weather Analyst assesses forecast uncertainty and communicates conditions that could affect access, lifting, or work at height.
S766: The Weather Service and Metocean Buoy provide inputs that are reviewed alongside direct observations from offshore personnel.
S767: The SCADA Gateway carries operational data to the Shore Control Room and preserves source timestamps where available.
